title: PET/CT radiomics predicted two-year outcomes in Hodgkin lymphoma
summary: In 289 patients with classical Hodgkin lymphoma, pretreatment PET/CT radiomics models predicted two-year event-free survival. The best ridge model had mean test AUC 0.81 (±0.12), with no significant advantage over a clinical/metabolic-tumour-volume logistic model. The retrospective single-institution study does not establish clinical utility; the first located result-bearing public version is the 2022-08-25 journal article.
ai_technology: Seven machine-learning models on FDG PET/CT radiomics; ridge regression performed best
organization: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust; University of Leeds; University of Oxford

evidence.tested: Retrospective single-institution cohort split into training (231) and test (58), with stratified five-fold tuning; no external prospective validation.
evidence.unknown: No independent, prospective or clinical-impact evaluation is reported unless specified in the tested field.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models used pretreatment PET/CT radiomic features to estimate two-year event-free survival.
